subject.title: Feature: fallbackChannel for hook mappings when primary delivery fails

question: Should hook mappings gain an explicit ordered post-failure delivery fallback contract, and if so must every fallback target include its own explicit recipient/account/thread identity rather than inheriting the primary route?
rationale: The request adds durable configuration and changes where hook-derived content may be sent after a failure; source and docs show that existing `bestEffortDeliver` and `failureDestination` have different semantics, so implementation cannot safely choose the privacy, retry, and duplicate-delivery policy alone.

options.title: Design explicit ordered fallback targets
options.body: Add a bounded typed fallback-target list with explicit routing identity, definitive-failure rules, dedupe, and focused migration-free regression coverage.

options.title: Keep one delivery target
options.body: Retain the existing single-route hook contract and direct operators to failure notifications or channel recovery rather than replaying the response elsewhere.

options.title: Expose only a failure alert
options.body: Extend failure reporting without resending the original hook response, avoiding cross-channel content replication while providing operator visibility.

recommendation.title: Design explicit ordered fallback targets
recommendation.body: Add a bounded typed fallback-target list with explicit routing identity, definitive-failure rules, dedupe, and focused migration-free regression coverage.
